methods.name: Peer-Median

methods.rationale: 5 same-sector peers exist in Drones & Autonomous, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Innoviz Technologies is a public-stage company in the Drones & Autonomous sector that completed an IPO. The comparable universe consists of five private peers operating in the same sector: Zipline, Joby Aviation, Nuro, Archer Aviation, and Elroy Air. No public peers exist within the narrowly defined Drones & Autonomous category.

A peer-median valuation approach was not applicable to this analysis. The Drones & Autonomous sector contains only five companies total, and filtering for same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-valuation-tier comparables yielded zero datapoints meeting the minimum threshold of three peers. Relying on an all-sector median would introduce substantial noise given the heterogeneity of business models, maturity levels, and capital requirements across the five available private companies. The absence of public comparables further limits triangulation to observable market transactions and precedent financings within the peer set.

Without sufficient comparable datapoints meeting established filters, this valuation cannot be supported by standard peer-multiple methodologies. A credible range would require alternative approaches—such as discounted cash flow analysis, precedent transaction analysis within the five-company private set, or detailed financing history of the five peers—none of which are present in the available data. The key uncertainty remains the lack of sufficient narrow comparables to establish reliable multiples for either revenue or EBITDA-based valuation frameworks.
